actions.name: Compromise thousands of Internet-connected devices including SOHO routers, firewalls, NAS, and IoT devices
actions.description: People’s Republic of China (PRC)-linked cyber actors have compromised thousands of Internet-connected devices, including small office/home office (SOHO) routers, firewalls, network-attached storage (NAS) and Internet of Things (IoT) devices with the goal of creating a network of compromised nodes (a “botnet”) positioned for malicious activity.

actions.name: Use botnet as a proxy to conceal identities while deploying DDoS attacks or compromising targeted U.S. networks
actions.description: The actors may then use the botnet as a proxy to conceal their identities while deploying distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks or compromising targeted U.S. networks.

actions.name: Control and manage a botnet active since mid-2021
actions.description: Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), a PRC-based company, has controlled and managed a botnet active since mid-2021.

actions.name: Maintain botnet with tens to hundreds of thousands of compromised devices
actions.description: The botnet has regularly maintained between tens to hundreds of thousands of compromised devices.

actions.name: Botnet consisted of over 260,000 devices as of June 2024
actions.description: As of June 2024, the botnet consisted of over 260,000 devices.

actions.name: Use China Unicom Beijing Province Network IP addresses to control and manage the botnet
actions.description: Integrity Tech has used China Unicom Beijing Province Network IP addresses to control and manage the botnet described in this advisory.

actions.name: Use China Unicom Beijing Province Network IP addresses to access other operational infrastructure for computer intrusion activities against U.S. victims
actions.description: These same China Unicom Beijing Province Network IP addresses were used to access other operational infrastructure employed in computer intrusion activities against U.S. victims.

actions.name: Use tactics, techniques, and infrastructure associated with Flax Typhoon, RedJuliett, and Ethereal Panda
actions.description: FBI found activity consistent with the tactics, techniques, and infrastructure associated with the cyber threat group known publicly as Flax Typhoon, RedJuliett, and Ethereal Panda.

actions.name: Compromise Internet-connected devices using known vulnerability exploits
actions.description: To recruit a new “bot,” the botnet system first compromises an Internet-connected device using one of a variety of known vulnerability exploits.

actions.name: Execute Mirai-based malware payload from a remote server on compromised devices
actions.description: Post-compromise, the victim device executes a Mirai-based malware payload from a remote server.

actions.name: Establish connection with command-and-control server using TLS on port 443
actions.description: Once executed, the payload starts processes on the device to establish a connection with a command-and-control (C2) server using Transport Layer Security (TLS) on port 443.

actions.name: Gather system information from infected devices for enumeration
actions.description: The processes gather system information from the infected device, including but not limited to the operating system version and processor, memory and bandwidth details to send to the C2 server for enumeration purposes.

actions.name: Make requests to c.speedtest.net to gather additional Internet connection details
actions.description: The malware also makes requests to “c.speedtest.net,” likely to gather additional Internet connection details.

actions.name: Use self-deleting malware payloads to evade detection
actions.description: Some malware payloads were self-deleting to evade detection.

actions.name: Use subdomains of w8510.com as botnet command and control servers
actions.description: A variety of subdomains of “w8510.com” were linked to the botnet’s C2 servers. As of September 2024, investigators identified over 80 subdomains associated with w8510.com.

actions.name: Manage botnet’s C2 servers using upstream management servers on TCP port 34125
actions.description: A tier of upstream management servers using TCP port 34125 manage the botnet’s C2 servers.

actions.name: Host MySQL database on management servers storing over 1.2 million records of compromised devices
actions.description: These management servers host a MySQL database which stored information used for the control of the botnet. As of June 2024, this database contained over 1.2 million records of compromised devices, including over 385,000 unique U.S. victim devices, both previously and actively exploited.

actions.name: Host Sparrow application on management servers to interact with the botnet
actions.description: The management servers hosted an application known as “Sparrow,” which allows users to interact with the botnet.

actions.name: Access Sparrow application using China Unicom Beijing Province Network IP addresses
actions.description: The actors used specific IP addresses registered to China Unicom Beijing Province Network to access this application, including the same IP addresses previously used by Flax Typhoon to access the systems used in computer intrusion activities against U.S.-based victims.

actions.name: Use Sparrow application functions to manage and control the botnet and C2 servers
actions.description: The code for the Sparrow application, stored within a Git repository, defines functions that allow registered users to manage and control the botnet and C2 servers, sending tasks to victim devices including DDoS and exploitation commands to grow the botnet.

actions.name: Provide device vulnerability information and exploit capabilities via Sparrow application
actions.description: Sparrow also contains functionality providing device vulnerability information to users. A subcomponent called “vulnerability arsenal” also allows users to exploit traditional computer networks through the victim devices in the botnet.
